Population-level predictions from a per-row INLA fit

Source: R/methods_inla.R, R/predict_new_levels.R
predict.flexybayes_inla.Rd

Fixed-effect (population-level) predictions: the linear predictor is X beta with random effects held at their population mean (zero). On the identity link the response- and link-scale predictions coincide. This is the prediction surface marginaleffects uses for average predictions and slopes.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'flexybayes_inla'
predict(
  object,
  newdata = NULL,
  type = c("response", "link"),
  se.fit = FALSE,
  classify = NULL,
  level = 0.95,
  allow_new_levels = FALSE,
  mean_by = NULL,
  n_draws = 1000L,
  re_formula = NA,
  summary = TRUE,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'fb_predict_new'
print(x, digits = 4L, ...)

Arguments

object

A flexybayes_inla fit.

newdata

Optional data frame. Defaults to the fit data. Ignored, with a warning, when classify is supplied. On a model with an offset() the prediction includes the offset evaluated on newdata, so newdata needs every column the offset reads. An absent one refuses with newdata_offset_missing instead of being taken as zero.

type

"response" or "link".

se.fit

Logical: also return delta-method standard errors from the fixed-effect covariance.

classify

The factors to break a predicted-value table down by: a character value ("Variety", "Variety:env") or a one-sided formula (~ Variety). The factors may be fixed or random. NULL (the default) is the historical behaviour.

level

Credible level for the classify table's interval, or for the predictive interval with allow_new_levels = TRUE, as a proportion. Default 0.95.

allow_new_levels

Logical. FALSE (the default) is the population-level prediction above. TRUE returns the posterior predictive of the rows of newdata (see Details), in which every random effect enters: a level the fit saw at its posterior draw, and a level it did not see drawn from its fitted variance component.

mean_by

With allow_new_levels = TRUE, the columns of newdata whose combinations define the sets of rows to average: a character vector or a one-sided formula. mean_by = ~ TRIAL predicts each trial mean, ~ TRIAL + VARIETY + NRATE each cell mean. NULL (the default) predicts each row.

n_draws

With allow_new_levels = TRUE, the number of posterior draws. Default 1000.

re_formula

NA (the default): the prediction is population-level, the fixed part of the model, as re_formula = NA gives on a brms fit. Any other value refuses with method_argument_not_supported. fitted() returns the predictions at the fitted levels of the random effects.

summary

TRUE (the default): the prediction is the posterior mean. FALSE refuses with method_argument_not_supported. fb_as_draws_simple() returns the posterior draws.

...

Ignored, except that an argument of ASReml's predict() given with classify is refused by name.

x

An fb_predict_new table, printed with a banner naming what its numbers are.

digits

Number of significant digits for the printed table.

Value

With classify, a data frame of class fb_predict_classify. With allow_new_levels = TRUE, a data frame of class fb_predict_new: one row per set, holding the mean_by columns (or row), n_rows, estimate, sd, lower and upper (and status on a fit with fixed_alias = "drop", where a set holding a row the fit does not estimate is NA), with the joint predictive draws, draws by sets, in attr(, "draws"). Otherwise a numeric vector of predictions, or a list fit / se.fit when se.fit = TRUE.

Details

With gen random, classify = "gen" returns each genotype's fixed part plus its random effect, and on a multi-environment fit with gen:env random it also adds that genotype's gen:env effects averaged over environments. This matches ASReml's default predict(): equal-weight averaging over the fixed-term variables not in classify, a covariate held at its mean, variables that appear only in random terms ignored, and every random term whose variables are all in classify or averaged over included. The intervals integrate over INLA's hyperparameter configurations, so they include the uncertainty in the variance components. A table with no random term is computed by emmeans, with intervals from the Gaussian approximation of the fixed-effect posterior. The arguments of ASReml's predict() that change these rules (present, average, ignore, use, except, only, associate, levels, vcov, sed, parallel, aliased, design.points) are refused with classify_argument_not_supported.

With allow_new_levels = TRUE, the prediction for a set of rows is the mean response over them, observation noise included, as an observed trial or cell mean at a new locality would be. Given one posterior draw it is normal, with mean x'beta averaged over the rows plus the mean of the effects at levels the fit saw, and variance the sum over random terms of sigma^2 * sum_l (n_l / n)^2 over the unseen levels l (n_l of the n rows at level l), plus sigma_field^2 times the mean AR1 x AR1 correlation over pairs of rows in a trial the fit did not see, plus the residual variance over n. The prediction is the mixture of these normals over the draws: estimate and sd are its exact mean and standard deviation, and lower and upper its quantiles. The fixed effects and the seen effects are drawn jointly from INLA's approximation, and the variances from their continuous joint posterior (as fb_variance_draws() draws them). Every random number comes from R's generator, so set.seed() before the call makes the result repeatable.

The new-level draw is built for random intercepts, interactions (TRIAL:REP), diag(f):g and id(trial):ar1(row):ar1(col), over an independent residual or dsum(~ units | f), for a Gaussian response on the identity link. Any other structure is refused with predict_new_levels_structure_not_supported, a new level with no fitted variance (a new level of f in diag(f):g, a new residual section, a row or column off the fitted lattice) with predict_new_levels_no_variance, and another family with predict_new_levels_family_not_supported.

On a fit with fixed_alias = "drop", a row that is not a linear combination of the rows the model was fitted to has no estimable prediction: it is returned as NA, and the status attribute (a status element with se.fit = TRUE, a status column with classify) reads "Aliased" there and "Estimable" elsewhere, as in asreml's predict().
